answer: A sybil-resistant economy can require each agent to lock a small refundable stake before it can earn, so creating thousands of hollow identities stops paying: every fake costs real capital that only returns after honest work. A public reputation ledger then tracks the pulse of completed tasks for each identity over time, and only accounts with a sustained copper-solid history of verified contributions gain higher earning weight, making cheap mass forgery unprofitable while honest newcomers can still build trust gradually.
